place.en: Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Bei prefectures

outcome.en: left the Zhaoyi Army circuit with only two prefectures

claims.outcome: thereafter the five prefectures were served by two Zhaoyi circuits

translationRepairs: The Xiang–Wei six-prefecture circuit received the title Zhaoyi Army circuit; later Tian Chengsi seized four of its prefectures, leaving only two.
The Xiang–Wei six-prefecture circuit received the title Zhaoyi Army circuit; later Tian Chengsi seized Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Bei prefectures—four in all—leaving only two.

s0121 names the seized prefectures as 相、衛、洺、貝四州; the idiomatic summary “four of its prefectures” drops those explicit place names. Restoring Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Bei matches the Chinese list and the unit’s literal rendering.
The Youzhou deputy military commissioner concurrently led the Pinglu Army deputy military commissioner, with seat at Shunhua Prefecture.
The Youzhou deputy military commissioner concurrently served as Pinglu Army deputy military commissioner, with seat at Shunhua Prefecture.
In 幽州節度副使領平盧軍節度副使, 領 marks concurrent tenure of the Pinglu deputy commissionership, not command over that office as an object. “Served as” matches the administrative sense and the idiomatic field.
The Youzhou circuit concurrently served as frontier commissioner of its home prefecture and army, and also as grand commissioner over all Hebei forces.
The Youzhou military commissioner concurrently served as frontier commissioner of his home prefecture and army, and also as grand commissioner over all Hebei forces.

幽州節度 is the military commissioner (節度使), the person who 兼 holds further posts; rendering the subject as “Youzhou circuit” with “its” misattributes the officeholder. “Military commissioner” and “his” align with the Chinese and the idiomatic field.
An observation commissioner for Ping, Ying, Mo, and neighboring prefectures was appointed.
An observation commissioner for Ping, Ying Prefecture, a second Ying Prefecture, Mo, and neighboring prefectures was appointed.

置平、營、瀛、莫等州 lists four prefectures; the idiomatic text omits 營. The proposal’s undifferentiated “Ying, Ying” restores the count but still collapses two distinct places both romanized Ying; marking the latter as a second Ying Prefecture keeps both without Chinese in the English.
The observation commissioner for Ping, Ying, Ying, Mo, and other prefectures was established.
The observation commissioner for Ping, Ying Prefecture, a second Ying Prefecture, Mo, and other prefectures was established.

The literal already has two Ying forms for 營 and 瀛 but does not mark which is which. Calling the latter a second Ying Prefecture distinguishes the two places without Chinese characters or the proposed “Ying (Yingzhou …)” wording.
